chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who shoots at the hunted prey while he is on the mountain, so the arrow pierces it until it exits from the other side. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But if it falls into water or tumbles from the mountain and dies, do not eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game hunted with an arrow if it falls into water or dies from the fall?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the permissibility of game depends on the cause of death relative to the hunting act; if the arrow causes the death directly on land, the meat is halal, but if the prey dies from the impact of falling or submerging before retrieval, it is considered *maytah* (dead by natural causes). This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the hunter's intent and the immediate efficacy of the weapon in ensuring a swift, clean death.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Sama’at Bin Mahran who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who shoots at the hunted prey, and he is upon the mountain, so the arrow pierces it until he exits from the other side. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Eat it, but if it had fallen into the water, or tumbles from the mountain, so it dies, so do not eat it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who shoots a prey from the mountain and the arrow pierces through and comes out from the other side. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can use it for food. ‘He (the Imam) said, ‘If it falls in water or rolls down the mountain and dies then do not use it for food.’”
